headline: Tabled South Colony Road apartment and mixed-use projects and a Hall Avenue parking lot extension; approved a fence at 23A Country Way.
summary: Applicants asked to table plans for 358 Hall Avenue and two South Colony Road sites. Mr. Velez wants more engineering review before recommending on the South Colony Road sites, which sit near wetlands and Wharton Brook. A bond for 932 Northrop Road was also released.
decisions: Approved the October 7, 2026 meeting minutes, 4-0 with one abstention.
Tabled the proposed parking lot extension at 358 Hall Avenue at the applicant's request.
Deemed the fence at 23A Country Way not a significant impact activity, 5-0.
Approved the fence at 23A Country Way, on the condition that the posts be hand-dug, 5-0.
Tabled the mixed-use development at 900, 902, 920 and 940 South Colony Road at the applicant's request.
Tabled the 66-unit apartment building at 1052 South Colony Road.
Approved the release of the bond for 932 Northrop Road, 5-0.

Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, November 4, 2026  Page 1 
Wallingford Inland Wetlands and Watercourses Commission 
 
Regular Meeting 
Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Robert F. Parisi Council Chambers 
Town Hall – 45 South Main Street, Wallingford, CT 
 
MINUTES 
 
Chair James Vitali called this Regular Meeting of the Wallingford Inland Wetlands and Watercourses 
Commission to order on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 7:01 p.m. in the Robert F. Parisi Council 
Chambers, Town Hall, 45 South Main Street, Wallingford, CT. 
 
PRESENT: Chair Vitali, Vice Chair Deborah Phillips; Secretary Nick Kern; Commissioner Michael Caruso; 
and Alternate Commissioners Aili McKeen and Caroline Raynis.  Also in attendance was Sebastian Velez, 
Environmental and Natural Resources Planner. 
 
ABSENT: Commissioner Jeffrey Necio and Alternate James Heilman. 
 
There were four people in the audience.  
 
A. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
The Pledge was recited. 
 
B. ROLL CALL 
As above. 
 
Chair Vitali stated that the voters tonight would be Commissioners Phillips, Kern, Caruso, McKeen, and 
himself. 
 
 
C. CONSIDERATION OF MINUTES 
1. Regular Meeting, October 7, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
 
MS. PHILLIPS: MOTION TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING OF OCTOBER 7, 2026.  
   
MR. CARUSO: SECOND. 
VOTE:  MR. CARUSO – YES; MS. PHILLIPS – ABSTAIN; MR. KERN – YES; MS. MCKEEN – YES;  
  CHAIR VITALI – YES.  
 
 
D. OLD BUSINESS 
1. #A26-7.6 /358 Hall Avenue / Jeffrey Laforge (Proposed Parking Lot Extension) 
Tabled at the request of the applicant. 
 
Mr. Velez explained that the applicant requested and consented to an extension. The signature of the 
property owner is missing. It is required by Regulation 7.4. He stated that he will check to see how many 
additional extensions are allowed.
Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, November 4, 2026  Page 2 
2. #A26-9.1 / 23A Country Way / Daniel Riley (Proposed fence) 
Mr. Velez reported that the proposed fence goes through a wetland area in the middle of the property 
according to an old survey.  The proposed fence is for a dog. He recommends that the application be 
tabled until we can get an updated delineation of the wetlands.  He also recommends that the applicant 
shift the fence into the upland review area. 
 
Appearing was Daniel Riley of 23A Country Way.  He explained that the wetland area is a swale that 
feeds into the woodlands. It’s grass that he mows regularly. The fence would cross the wetlands by 52 
linear feet.  Moving the fence back would eliminate the ability to bring the fence to the house. The fence 
will be a privacy fence on the right to the tree line, and the main portion will be a black vinyl chain link.  
The vinyl doesn’t need the six-inch holes of the privacy fence.  The contractor can install without going 
into the ground.   
 
Chair Vitale stated that his concern is the equipment that will be used.  Mr. Riley noted that he mows 
regularly and it doesn’t get muddy. He only saw water there once.  Chair Vitale stated that he doesn’t 
see any gain in moving the fence.  
 
Ms. McKee stated that the post holes can be dug by hand. 
 
Mr. Kern stated that he would rather the fence be put in with posts into the ground.   
 
Ms. Phillips stated that if the holes are hand-dug, there will be little impact.   
 
Mr. Riley noted that the plan is to hand dig.  
 
Chair Vitali confirmed that the Commission is not interested in tabling the application. 
 
Chair Vitali called for a motion regarding significant activity. 
 
MS. PHILLIPS: MOTION TO APPROVE APPLICATION #A26-9.1 / 23A COUNTRY WAY /DANIEL RILEY BE  
  DEEMED NOT A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ACTIVITY. 
 
MR. CARUSO: SECOND 
VOTE:  MS. PHILLIPS – YES; MR. KERN – YES; MR. CARUSO – YES; MS. MCKEEN – YES; CHAIR 
VITALI – YES. 
 
Chair Vitali confirmed that the applicant is willing to make the installation of the posts be hand-dug a 
condition of approval. 
 
MS. PHILLIPS: MOTION TO APPROVE APPLICATION #A26-9.1 / 23A COUNTRY WAY /DANIEL RILEY  
  (PROPOSED FENCE) WITH THE CONDITION THAT THE FENCE POSTS ARE HAND-DUG. 
 
MR. HEILMAN: SECOND 
VOTE:  MS. PHILLIPS – YES; MR. KERN – YES; MR. CARUSO – YES; MS. MCKEEN – YES; CHAIR 
VITALI – YES. 
 
Mr. Kern suggested that Wetlands plaques be placed on the fence. Mr. Velez said he would provide 
them.
Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, November 4, 2026  Page 3 
 
3. #A26-10.1 /900/902/920/940 So. Colony Road / Dominic DeMartino (Mixed-use development) 
And 
5. #A26-10.2 / 1052 So. Colony Road / Dominic DeMartino (66 Unit Apartment Building with 
associated parking and landscaping) 
Mr. Velez stated that the applicant requested that the applications be tabled. He stated that there are a 
few things missing from the 900- 940 application. He noted that the application for 1052 is more 
complete. He is waiting for a response from the engineer and has no recommendation yet.  
 
Chair Vitali noted that the applicant stated that there will be no impact to the wetlands, but that is not 
up to the applicant.   
 
Mr. Velez stated that the drainage report indicates that the proposal won’t increase it, but he still wants 
the engineering review.  Behind both properties are wetlands and Wharton Brook.  He would like more 
information. 
 
Chair Vitali clarified that both applications are being tabled. Mr. Velez confirmed. 
 
 
E. NEW BUSINESS 
None 
 
 
F. REPORTS & COMMUNICATIONS 
1. Restoration Monitoring Status Report for Soil Remediation Project at 5 and 21 Toelles Road 
dated October 7, 2026 (A20-7.1) 
Mr. Velez reported that the report was in the packet and that he visited the site.  The restoration looks 
beautiful. He agreed with the conclusions in the report. 
 
2. Staff Memo for Bond Release Request for 932 Northrop Road dated 10/14/26. 
Mr. Velez reported that he went to the site and the silt fence has been removed and the site looks great. 
He recommends releasing the bond. 
 
MS. PHILLIPS: MOTION TO RELEASE THE BOND FOR 932 NORTHROP ROAD. 
 
MR. CARUSO: SECOND 
VOTE:  MS. PHILLIPS – YES; MR. KERN – YES; MR. CARUSO – YES; MS. MCKEEN – YES; CHAIR 
VITALI – YES. 
 
3. 60 Carpenter Lane Sediment and Erosion Control (#A26-6.1)/Staff Memo dated 10/29/26 
Mr. Velez reported that he has been to the site several times, including with the Town Planner and the 
new Zoning Enforcement Officer.  There is no sediment or erosion in the upland review area or the 
wetland area that is abutting this property, but there are erosion issues on the site.  He has spoken to 
the Legal Department and sent a Notice of Violation because they are not following the erosion control 
plan. That was sent today. 
 
Chair Vitali asked if the erosion controls were put in place. Mr. Velez replied that there are controls at 
the site but not as approved by the Commission.  The applicant is not conforming to what was in the
Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, November 4, 2026  Page 4 
plan.  Some erosion controls have not been put in yet.  Chair Vitali asked if this Commission has 
jurisdiction.  Mr. Velez replied that he has spoken to the Legal Department. Since this Commission 
approved the plans, the applicant has to abide by them. 
 
4. Choate Carr Hall and Football Field 
Mr. Velez reported that Choate agreed to provide an updated drainage report. 
 
5. 360 Woodhouse Ave (#A26-4.1) status report 
Mr. Velez reported that he was notified that work started on the permit.  The owners have removed the 
pipe that was sending water to the wetlands.  The remaining pipe was deviated to the western side of 
the site. He has visited the site and met with the owner. The pipe that they just made is still off from the 
plan.  He reached out to their engineer.  The applicant may need to survey the pipe again and move it to 
what was approved on the plan.   
 
 
G. VIOLATIONS – discussion, hearing, and/or action 
none 
 
 
H. VIOLATIONS – pending (no action requested at this time) 
1. Notice of Violation Remains – 1245 Old Colony road & Quinnipiac River – Jerzy Pytel – 
(unpermitted clearing & filling near river) issued 6/4/19; NOV to be recorded on Land Records 
per 10/4/23 action; NOV affirmed 12/3/25 
 
2. Cease and Desist Order Remains – 250 Cook Hill Road – (unpermitted alteration of wetlands, 
installation of structures in or near wetlands, deposition of a significant amount of fill material 
in Upland Review Area) – issued 4/14/26; Order affirmed 4/22/26; Staff Memo Update on 
Violation 10/1/26 
 
Mr. Velez reported that the department has exhausted all options for enforcement and is talking to the 
Legal Department. There is still a lack of compliance. 
 
Chair Vitali noted that this Commission can’t impose fines. He noted that Planning and Zoning has a rule 
for the amount of fill without a permit.  Maybe they can get involved. 
 
3. Notice of Violation Remains – 24 Mapleview Road – Patricia Clarke c/o James W. & Patricia 
Clarke, Trustee of The Clarke 2022 Living Trust – (alteration & filling within wetlands and in 
Upland Review Area on 24 Mapleview Rd. & on 13 Rolling Meadow Dr.) issued 4/21/23; NOV 
affirmed 12/3/25. 
 
Chair Vitali commented on the packets that were distributed.   
 
 
I. NEXT SCHEDULED REGULAR MEETING:  December 2, 2026 
 
 
J. ADJOURNMENT
Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, November 4, 2026  Page 5 
MS. PHILLIPS: MOTION TO ADJOURN 
MR. CARUSO: SECOND 
VOTE:  THE MOTION WAS APPROVED BY ALL IN A VOICE VOTE. 
 
The Meeting was adjourned at 7:30 p.m. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Cheryl-Ann Tubby 
Recording Secretary
